findings.title: Redirect-follow loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000, breaking deep segment trees
findings.body: The loop bound was tightened from 10000 to 1000 while the explanatory comment about depth-10k trees was deleted. The redirect hash chain can still legitimately reach depths above 1000 (the data didn't change), so once `redirect_depth >= 1000` the loop exits early without resolving to a fixed point. The script then writes a `hset` mapping this span's id to an unresolved intermediate `set_span_id` and unions it into the wrong set, so subsequent children of the segment will land in a different buffer key. Result: spans get split across multiple `span-buf:s:*` keys instead of being joined into one segment — segments will be flushed incomplete or duplicated, directly causing data loss/duplication. The previous bound (and its comment) should be preserved unless the maximum possible redirect depth has been proven to be bounded below 1000.

findings.title: Spans are silently evicted at insert time without any metric or log
findings.body: After merging incoming spans into `set_key`, the script does `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call('zpopmin', set_key, span_count - 1000) end`. There is no `redis.call('incrby', ...)` for a metric, no log, and the corresponding `metrics.incr('spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded')` was removed from `_load_segment_data`. Spans are silently dropped from the segment with zero observability. Worse, the eviction is by lowest `end_timestamp_precise` score, which is not necessarily the spans that are safe to drop (a parent span sent late would have a later score than its children and be kept, while a root span sent early could be evicted, leaving the segment without a root and causing it to fall through to the long `span_buffer_timeout_secs` path or be flushed incomplete). The threshold 1000 also does not match `max_segment_spans=1001` configured on `SpansBuffer`. At minimum this needs a counter (e.g. `metrics.incr('spans.buffer.evicted', n)`), a log when eviction occurs, and a guarantee that the root span (or HRS flag) is preserved.

findings.title: Negative offset slice on Django QuerySet raises AssertionError
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (a negative int) when `enable_advanced_features` is True. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` asserts `k.start >= 0` and raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` for any negative start index, so this path can never produce results. The cursor string is parsed by `Cursor.from_string` via `int(bits[1])`, which happily accepts a negative value, so any client (or a hand-crafted cursor) can trigger the crash. Combined with the `organization_auditlogs.py` change that always passes `enable_advanced_features=True` for superusers/admins, the new admin endpoint is a guaranteed `AssertionError` whenever the resulting cursor has offset < 0.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator has no working behavior beyond BasePaginator
findings.body: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class duplicates almost all of `BasePaginator.get_result` and the only behavior change is the negative-offset branch. Because that branch cannot work (Django rejects negative slicing, see other finding), `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is functionally identical to `BasePaginator`. The `enable_advanced_features=True` flag exposed via `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` therefore does nothing useful in production. The PR title is 'Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert'; this entire paginator/auditlog change is unrelated and should be split out. As shipped it adds dead code, a misleading admin-only API knob, and a guaranteed crash path.

findings.title: Required `end_timestamp_precise` field added to Span NamedTuple is a contract break
findings.body: `Span` is a public NamedTuple. Adding `end_timestamp_precise: float` before the defaulted `is_segment_span: bool = False` makes it a required positional argument and breaks every existing `Span(...)` call site that does not supply it (TypeError). All in-repo callers in this PR are updated, but there are likely other consumers (snuba-spans ingestion, tests outside this PR, downstream internal tools) that construct `Span` instances directly. Any such caller will now crash at module/import time on first use, and any older serialized payload that doesn't carry `end_timestamp_precise` will now KeyError inside `process_batch`. This change should either default to `0.0`/`None` or have a clearly documented migration; missing-field handling in `process_batch` is not implemented.

findings.title: No test covers the new 1000-span eviction path
findings.body: Tests under `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py` and `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py` only ever add ~4 spans per segment. The new Lua eviction kicks in at >1000 spans, which is now the actual hard cap on segment size (the Python `max_segment_spans` check was removed), yet nothing exercises it. A test that ingests >1000 spans into one segment is needed to assert: (a) eviction actually happens, (b) the root span (or HRS flag) is preserved, (c) a metric is emitted so the silent-drop path is observable. Without this, regressions in the eviction behavior would land silently.

findings.title: Misleading 'Performance optimization' comment for a behavior change
findings.body: The change in `BasePaginator.get_result` from `results = list(queryset[offset:stop])` to `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` is a small behavioral fix, not a performance optimization. The new `max(0, offset)` call is essentially free and does not reduce query cost; it just prevents an `AssertionError` for negative non-prev cursors. The inline comment 'Performance optimization: For high-traffic scenarios, allow negative offsets...' is misleading and should describe the actual change (clamping negative non-prev offsets to 0 to avoid a crash). Also note the asymmetry: prev cursors are NOT clamped, so a negative prev cursor will still crash in Django — the two branches should behave consistently.

findings.title: ZADD uses payload bytes as member; duplicate payloads are silently dropped
findings.body: Switching the segment from `sadd` to `zadd` keeps the same 'member = span.payload (bytes)' model. Sorted sets require unique members, so two spans whose serialized payloads happen to be byte-identical (e.g. retries, duplicate Kafka messages, or same span replayed) will be collapsed to one entry on insertion. The Lua script's eviction then operates on this collapsed set, and the Python `_load_segment_data` will only see one copy. This is the same potential bug `sadd` had (it also dedups by member), but it is now more consequential because the score-based eviction changes ordering. Worth either documenting the assumption (that payloads are unique) or de-duplicating earlier so that eviction counts are meaningful.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE used with destination equal to one of its source keys
findings.body: `redis.call('zunionstore', set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)` and the analogous `set_key, 2, set_key, parent_key` pass `set_key` as both destination and source. While this happens to behave correctly in some single-instance Redis versions (because the source data is gathered before the destination is rewritten), it is not documented as a supported pattern, can produce non-deterministic results across versions, and is a footgun in cluster mode where slot routing must already match. The safer equivalent is: gather members via ZRANGE/ZRANGEBYSCORE, then ZADD them to `set_key` (or union into a temp key and RENAME). At minimum this should be commented and pinned against a tested Redis version.

findings.title: Admin-only pagination branch wraps a broken paginator behind an undocumented query flag
findings.body: `use_optimized = request.GET.get('optimized_pagination') == 'true'` enables `OptimizedCursorPaginator` for superusers/org members with global access. Because the paginator's only distinguishing behavior (negative offsets) crashes Django (see paginator.py finding), the branch serves no purpose other than to expose a new failure mode. There is no test in this PR for the new branch, no documentation/changelog entry, and no consumer that actually needs negative offsets. This is dead/unsafe code shipped under an unrelated PR title; it should be reverted from this PR and either fixed properly or removed.
